answer: A claim of uniqueness must be accompanied by a proof that no other identity holds the same underlying resource. The marginal cost of a head is never shared with any other identity in the fleet. The ridge is the unique resource, the sonnet the proof that excludes every other holder, and the nectar the registry that makes the exclusion checkable; cloning the ridge forces two contradictory sonnet proofs, and the nectar is where the contradiction shows.
